lines.trans: Maxim, come over here quickly.
You are here like a silent reproach from the past.
Tell me, do you want to fire me?
Yes, I want to very much, but I cannot.
After all, I gave my honest word.
Maxim, go work in the kitchen instead.
Our chef will not take me back.
Chef, you look very good today.
Did you dress up so nicely for a wedding?
No, I dressed up for a funeral.
Vitya, why is your cook walking around in the hall?
Because I kicked him out of the kitchen.

examples.trans: May I go to the restroom first?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'тому').

examples.text: Потому что я его с кухни выгнал.
examples.trans: Because I kicked him out of the kitchen.

examples.text: Потому что у нас сегодня важный банкет.
examples.trans: Because we have an important banquet today.

examples.text: Я же с половины спектакля не бегаю, потому что друзья приехали.
examples.trans: After all, I do not run out halfway through a play because friends arrived.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я надеюсь, что у нас есть целая жизнь.
examples.trans: I hope that we have a whole life.

examples.text: Сказал, что его блюда едят только в ресторане.
examples.trans: He said that his dishes are eaten only in the restaurant.

examples.text: Потому что я его с кухни выгнал.
examples.trans: Because I kicked him out of the kitchen.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'his', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Если, конечно, футбол тебе дороже, чем я.
examples.trans: If, of course, football is dearer to you than I am.

examples.text: Вот как с ним бороться, я не понимаю.
examples.trans: How to deal with him, I do not understand.

examples.text: Я тоже не понимаю, встречаемся мы или нет.
examples.trans: I also do not understand whether we are dating or not.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with / from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Если, конечно, футбол тебе дороже, чем я.
examples.trans: If, of course, football is dearer to you than I am.

examples.text: Хорошо, милая, как скажешь, так и будет.
examples.trans: Alright, darling, as you say, so it will be.

examples.text: Дмитрий Владимирович, у вас есть минутка?
examples.trans: Dmitry Vladimirovich, do you have a minute?

meanings.en: to kick out, to drive out
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'гнать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'kicked out / drove out', paired with 'выгонять'.

examples.text: Потому что я его с кухни выгнал.
examples.trans: Because I kicked him out of the kitchen.

examples.text: А меня она выгонит!
examples.trans: She will kick me out!

examples.text: Для тебя она добрая. А меня она выгонит!
examples.trans: She's kind to you. But she'll kick me out!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'back / ago', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Возьми его обратно назад!
examples.trans: Take him back again!

examples.text: А я час назад был уборщиком, сейчас курьер, а к вечеру могу снова поваром стать.
examples.trans: And an hour ago I was a cleaner, now a courier, and by evening I can become a cook again.

examples.text: Я их ещё два года назад им выделил!
examples.trans: I allocated it to them two years ago!
